records.text: Privateer Groy is a blunt, impatient dockside privateer preoccupied with delayed shipments. When an Akiris delivery reaches him, he carefully inspects Bloads’s bundle, pays the courier, and tells them to get off his docks; his ambient remarks blame couriers for keeping him waiting.
Baldruc is a Gryphon Master whose menu offers flight routes. When attacked, he calls for guards and summons an enraged gryphon.
A Searing Hatchling is a young dragonkin found in Dustwallow Marsh. It casts a spell in combat.
A Searing Whelp is a young dragonkin found in Dustwallow Marsh. It casts a spell in combat.
Firemane Scalebanes are among the targets Tharg names in his campaign against the black dragons. The Scalebane’s combat behavior includes Fire Shield, Shield Bash, and Sunder Armor.
A Firemane Scout is a dragonkin combatant encountered in Dustwallow Marsh. Tharg's request names Firemane Scouts among its targets, and this one can disappear when struck by a spell.
A Firemane Ash Tail is a dragonkin combatant found in Dustwallow Marsh and named among the targets in Tharg's request. It uses Fire Nova in combat and can disappear when struck by a spell.
Firemane Flamecallers are dragonkin combatants found in Dustwallow Marsh. This flamecaller casts Fireball when engaged.
Brimgore is a named dragonkin elite encountered in Dustwallow Marsh. It uses distinct abilities during combat and when injured.
Drywallow Crocolisks are beasts found across several areas of the region.
Drywallow Snappers are beasts found in two areas of the region.
A Noxious Flayer is a creature of Dustwallow Marsh, found across several of its areas. It casts a spell in combat.
A Noxious Reaver is a creature of Dustwallow Marsh, found in a few of its areas. It casts a spell in combat.
A Noxious Shredder is a creature of Dustwallow Marsh, found across several of its areas. It casts a spell in combat.
Bloodfen Razormaws are beasts found around the Bloodfen wetlands. They use a combat spell when fighting.
Bloodfen Lashtails are beasts found around the Bloodfen wetlands. They use a combat spell when fighting.
Mirefin Murlocs inhabit Dustwallow Marsh. These murlocs may flee for assistance when badly hurt.
Mirefin Muckdwellers are murlocs of Dustwallow Marsh. They cast a spell when a fight begins.
Mirefin Coastrunners are murlocs found in Dustwallow Marsh. In combat, they use Piercing Strike.
Mirefin Oracles are murlocs found in Dustwallow Marsh.
Strashaz Warriors are humanoid combatants. They use a combat spell.
Strashaz Serpent Guards are humanoid combatants. They use a combat spell.
A Strashaz Myrmidon is a martial combatant of the Strashaz group.
A Strashaz Sorceress is a combatant of the Strashaz group, with several abilities used during a fight, including when engaged and as her health falls.
A Strashaz Siren is a combatant of the Strashaz group. She uses a combat ability.
A Strashaz Hydra is a combat creature in the Strashaz group. It uses an ability in combat.
Darkmist Spiders are ordinary hostile spiders found across two areas. In combat they can use Poison.
Darkmist Recluses are hostile spider creatures found in two areas. They use a combat ability.
Darkmist Silkspinners are hostile spider creatures found in three areas. They use an ability in combat.
The Darkmist Widow is a spider creature, notable for its powerful build and venomous attacks.
Withervine Creepers are hostile plant-like creatures found in three areas. In combat they use Creeping Vines.
A Withervine Rager is a hostile elemental found in the wetlands. When badly hurt, it can flare into a sudden rage, a reaction marked by its enraged cry.
Withervine Mire Beasts are hostile marsh creatures. They lash out with a spell as they weaken, making an injured beast especially dangerous to approach.
Young Murk Threshers are aquatic animals that inhabit the wetlands. They are the younger members of the local thresher population.
Murk Threshers are aquatic animals found in the wetlands. They are the mature form of the local thresher population, larger than the young threshers.
Elder Murk Threshers are older members of the thresher population in the wetlands. Their name marks an age distinction from ordinary Murk Threshers.
Mudrock Spikeshells are hostile aquatic animals found in the wetlands. They defend themselves with a spiked attack when threatened.
Muckshell Clackers are creatures found in Dustwallow Marsh. A Clacker casts a spell while in combat.
Muckshell Pincers are creatures found in Dustwallow Marsh.
Muckshell Scrabblers are creatures found in Dustwallow Marsh. A Scrabbler casts spells in combat and when badly wounded.
Darkfang Creepers are spiders found across Dustwallow Marsh. In combat, a Creeper uses Slowing Poison.
Darkfang Venomspitters are spiders found across Dustwallow Marsh. A Venomspitter casts a spell when drawn into combat.
Giant Darkfang Spiders are spiders found in several parts of Dustwallow Marsh. In combat, a Giant Darkfang Spider uses Poison.

Overlord Mok'Morokk leads the Stonemaul ogres in Brackenwall after dragons drove them from their old home. He says Rexxar made him leader and insists he keeps the clan safe, yet Draz'Zilb accuses him of turning from leadership to demanding service after Rexxar left. Mok'Morokk prefers the new refuge and dismisses warnings about dragons; he also admits he fled so quickly that he left his belongings behind. He is still ready to boast and fight anyone who challenges his rule.

Draz'Zilb is an unusually articulate, learned ogre who investigates the dragon brood with arcane study of its scorched hearts and tongues. He is focused on identifying the source of the attacks and reclaiming Stonemaul Village, and openly condemns Mok'Morokk for ruling through demands instead of serving the clan. Draz'Zilb refuses to accept Brackenwall as a lasting home; his plans include challenging Mok'Morokk's leadership.

Tharg is an ogre of Stonemaul who remains in Brackenwall after Mok'Morokk led the ogres away from their southern home. Black dragons killed Tharg's wife, and he wants the ogres to fight them, take revenge, and reclaim Stonemaul Ruins rather than stay in the swamp.

Mudcrush Durtfeet is a hungry ogre in northern Dustwallow who asks for fish heads to eat. He warns that he may eat the player without food, then responds that he will not eat them after receiving the fish.

Nazeer Bloodpike directs Horde intelligence work from Brackenwall Village. He orders the removal of Theramore infiltrators and assigns the recovery of documents his spies lost after being discovered at the docks. He also receives the latest report from Horde agent Marg Nighteye, whose fate in the swamp appears uncertain.

“Swamp Eye” Jarl is an eccentric swamp cook whose appetite runs to unusual ingredients: he praises spider eyes as tasty, salty chicken and asks for frog legs for stew. He also seeks a particular sword for cutting, though he keeps the intended dish to himself. His blunt, food-focused manner comes through in his warning that he wants nothing unless he can eat it.

Morgan Stern is a cook in Theramore developing “Mudrock Soup and Bugs” for the Blue Recluse in Stormwind. Doubting he would survive hunting in Dustwallow Marsh, Morgan asks others for forked Mudrock tongues, whose flavor he wants to explore, and pristine crawler legs for presentation. Morgan experiments with cooking techniques and sends Stinky Ignatz for bogbean leaves. When told someone helped Ignatz escape trouble, Morgan thanks the helper and offers to ask his uncle to provide a feast on a future Blue Recluse visit.

Theramore Infiltrators are Alliance operatives positioned east of Brackenwall Village. Nazeer Bloodpike describes them as spying on the village and reporting Horde movements to Theramore, making their covert presence a target of Horde concern.

Deadmire is an ancient, enormous crocolisk in the Dustwallow Marsh. Though his aging body causes him constant, maddening pain, he retains the strength and speed of youth. The account of him calls him a noble creature with a powerful spirit.
Ogg'marr is a butcher who offers goods for sale. His role combines a practical food trade with a vendor service for visitors in the area.

“Stinky” Ignatz is a swamp-wise gatherer who takes paid work collecting bogbean leaves. He has separate arrangements with Mebok Mizzyrix, who needs leaves for a potion, and cook Morgan Stern, who is researching a recipe. When surrounded while searching, Ignatz asks for help and leads an escort through the herb search; at the end, he thanks his escort and directs them to his employer about a reward.
Krak is an armorer who sells goods and provides equipment repair. His services are presented as practical equipment support.

Zulrg is a weaponsmith with a goods service and repair service. His title identifies his trade specifically with weapons, distinguishing his counter from the armor and shield work offered by other smiths in the area.

Gregor MacVince is a horse breeder who offers horses for purchase. His dialogue presents careful breeding and care as the basis of his stock, and describes a horse as a companion. A separate conditional response says Stormwind expects exalted standing before selling its finest steeds; the condition does not establish any visitor's eligibility.
Hans Weston is an armorer and shieldsmith, with goods and repair services. His title points to armor and shields, setting his work apart from the area's weaponsmiths and gunsmith.

Marie Holdston is a weaponsmith who offers goods and repairs. Her title places her among the area's weapon specialists, alongside Zulrg, while the available evidence gives her no further individual distinction.

Torq Ironblast is a gunsmith with goods and repair services, and a quest-giver interaction. His title distinguishes his trade in firearms from the area's other smiths; the available evidence does not identify the subject or outcome of his quest interaction.

Piter Verance works as both a weaponsmith and armorer, offering goods and repairs. His combined title marks a broader armament trade than the area's smiths whose titles specify weapons or armor alone.
Dwane Wertle is a chef who offers goods for sale in the marsh settlement.
Jensen Farran is a bowyer who offers goods for sale, including ammunition, and provides repairs.
Bartender Lillian works as a bartender and offers goods for sale in the marsh settlement.
Craig Nollward is a cook who offers goods for sale in the marsh settlement.
Smiling Jim is remembered in a tavern song for bringing mead and beer and serving the people there year after year. The refrain calls him Smiling Jim.
Charity Mipsy sells general goods and offers ammunition in the marsh settlement.
Helenia Olden is a Trade Supplies vendor with goods to browse. She also has a questgiver role.
Brant Jasperbloom trains herbalism.
Uma Bartulm supplies Herbalism and Alchemy goods to customers.
Alchemist Narett trains Alchemy. He jokes that all the stirring builds strong arms, while noting he is no adventurer.
Sara Pierce is a humanoid in Dustwallow Marsh.
Mikal Pierce is a humanoid in Dustwallow Marsh.

Guard Byron is a Theramore guard who feels sorry for Smiling Jim. He remembers Jim’s former marsh inn as a wonderful place, but is reluctant to discuss what happened there and directs questions to Captain Garran Vimes.
A guard named Edward.
A guard named Jarad.
Combat Master Criton is a humanoid combat master in Dustwallow Marsh.

Krog is a Horde investigator in Brackenwall Village, pursuing the truth behind the Shady Rest Inn attack. He follows tracks and connects hoofprints and a shield marked by Mosarn to the Grimtotem, but treats that lead as suspicion rather than proof. He examines weapons and a battle plan, weighs what the Grimtotem intend toward the Horde, and is wary that questioning Mosarn could attract attention. Krog believes the evidence points to Grimtotem action against humans, yet leaves their intentions toward his own people unresolved. He reports the case to the Warchief and warns against discussing it until Thrall has acted.

Caz Twosprocket is one of Theramore's best blacksmiths. Examining a blackened iron shield, he says it is neither his work nor that of any blacksmith he knows on this side of the sea. He notices its burned-off leather strap and judges that the shield was made to fit someone large, perhaps a tauren, while admitting that is all he can tell. With Theramore's siege engines nearly complete, Caz says he is getting bored and invites visitors to compare engineering blueprints.

Captain Garran Vimes serves Theramore as a military investigator and organizer. He is pursuing the Shady Rest Inn destruction and the murder of the Hyal family, while gathering intelligence on deserters and suspected Horde spies. He shares leads with his trackers and patrols, and speaks plainly about the danger beyond his soldiers’ protection. After the Hyal family’s killers are brought to justice, he arranges a wreath for their grave and carries a message to James.

This Theramore lieutenant directs the orc spy report to Captain Garran Vimes, who is known to understand orcish. The lieutenant’s documented responsibility here is passing that warning up the chain about Horde spies near Theramore.

Adjutant Tesoran keeps Theramore's guard personnel and equipment records. When asked about Lieutenant Paval Reethe, he checks his books and identifies Reethe as a former recruit who joined the guard and is listed as missing.
Spot is a beast found in Dustwallow Marsh.
A Theramore guard engaged in practicing combat.

Commander Samaul leads Miss Proudmoore’s forces in Theramore and is loyal to her. Though occupied, he offers help courteously and keeps answers brief. He guards the marsh’s security closely, points investigators toward the tower where he believes Hendel was stationed, and warns travelers about dangers beyond the city.
Pained is a humanoid named Pained.

Private Hendel is a Theramore soldier assigned to guard infiltrators monitoring Brackenwall and threats to the border. He reports little progress and warns citizens about the danger. Accused of allying with the Defias, he reacts angrily; if overcome, he can try to flee, give up the chase when too injured, and beg Proudmoore for mercy, saying he did not mean to.

Archmage Tervosh serves Lady Proudmoore in Theramore and pursues arcane research, including experiments with shadowshard crystals. In the Missing Diplomat affair, he distrusts Private Hendel, judging his actions a betrayal, and coordinates with Proudmoore to locate and arrest him. Tervosh seeks to protect Theramore and have Hendel questioned; he also credits the traveler who helps prevent Hendel from escaping.

Lady Jaina Proudmoore rules Theramore and puts its people’s safety first while protecting the Alliance. Her diplomacy includes a secret summit between Thrall and King Wrynn. She investigates the Defias without committing forces that would leave her city vulnerable, and insists on confirming findings when their implications are grave.

Guard Lasiter is a Theramore guard who practices shooting at a target. He talks himself through adjusting his aim, acknowledging when he misses or barely hits and whether to correct to the right or left. A bullseye draws an excited reaction, suggesting a marksman still working through inconsistent shots.

Theramore’s guards keep watch over the city and hear out visitors. This guard welcomes newcomers and reads an altered leaflet distributed by Calia Hastings, reacting with disbelief and a joke about its claim that the deserters want a hair-gel fund.

Lieutenant Paval Reethe is a Theramore officer whose badge bears his name. Hiding amid the ruins and ash of Shady Rest, he first denies stealing from the inn or knowing about its fire. Under pressure from Ogron, he admits taking some supplies, then begins to explain what happened before breaking off at the sight of a girl with a weapon.

Ogron is a Brackenwall ogre who found the hiding Lieutenant Paval Reethe. He brings a companion along to question Reethe about the Shady Rest fire, pressing him with threats; during the search he also spots another fire and a human on a nearby island. Ogron speaks plainly and values a companion watching his back.
Theramore Deserters are humanoids found in Dustwallow Marsh.

Clerk Lendry handles inquiries at Foothold Citadel in Theramore. When asked about James Hyal, Lendry recalls the Shady Rest Inn incident and directs anyone with information to Captain Vimes, who is handling that investigation. This makes Lendry a local contact for the inquiry into James.
A Sentry Point Guard serves among the guards posted at Theramore's outpost in Dustwallow Marsh. The post lies near Dreadmurk Shore, where patrols have reported Defias survivors from a shipwreck.

Captain Wymor leads Theramore's inquiry at Sentry Point into Defias survivors from a wreck off the coast. He weighs scout reports and asks for help confirming who survived, then seeks their leader and orders. After receiving the orders, he suspects the cargo may have a wealthy patron and directs the search toward salvage diver Renn McGill.

Do'gol is a blacksmith in Brackenwall Village who examines a burned shield and spots writing along its rim. He asks for darkmist spider venom to clear it, then reads the name Mosarn and sends the investigator to Krog, whom he says knows many people. He makes shields rather than buying this one and admits he dislikes oversized spiders.

Balos Jacken is the deserters' lieutenant in Dustwallow Marsh. He says they expelled Reethe after Reethe kept raiding ogre supplies, a risk their small force could not withstand, and asks the visitor to forget the encounter in return for his help. When badly wounded, he surrenders and agrees to cooperate.
Combat Master Szigeti is a humanoid combat master in Dustwallow Marsh.
Guard Kahil is a humanoid guard.
A guard named Lana.
Narrisha serves as a guard.
Tark serves as a guard.
Captain Andrews is the Red Team’s captain.
Captain Thomas is the Blue Team’s captain.
Theramore sentries react to Proudmoore's arrival with warnings to run, fearing punishment from a woman if they are caught.
Medic Tamberlyn is a medic.
A medic named Helaina.
Ingo Woolybush is an Explorers' League member and questgiver.
The Coral Shark is an animal shark found across several areas in two regions.
Innkeeper Janene welcomes weary travelers to her inn and provides vendor service. She also offers a place to make their home and a seasonal Trick or Treat exchange.

Tabetha mentors spellcasters in Dustwallow Marsh, insisting on exact preparations for making a mage's wand. She can release a demon from a tainted summoner's orb, but expects the recipient to defeat it quickly and prepare for danger. She sets demanding trials that surprise her colleagues, and considers the nearby Grimtotems a persistent enemy of herself and her students.
Ghok'kah sells tailoring supplies.
Amie Pierce is a humanoid in Dustwallow Marsh.
Brother Karman is a paladin trainer. His greeting invokes the Light, and his training dialogue refers to learning its ways.

Captain Evencane is a warrior trainer in Theramore. He addresses training with the Theramore guard, placing his instruction in the city guard's context. He may tell a visitor he cannot train their class.
Zanara is a bowyer who offers goods for browsing and repair.
A Brackenwall enforcer in Dustwallow Marsh.
Michael is a stable master who helps adventurers stable their pets and recover lost companions.

Emberstrife, a child of Deathwing, tests candidates for ascension by sending them to kill champions of the rival dragonflights and bring back their skulls. He doubts Nefarian’s decision to send a whelp, but praises persistence and dedication when the tests are completed.
Timothy Worthington trains aspiring tailors. Proud of having outfitted kings, he presents proper training as a path to that level of skill.
Shardi is a wind rider master who helps travelers choose flight routes. When attacked, she calls for guards and summons an enraged wyvern.
Decedra Willham sits by the Great Sea and enjoys listening to its sounds. She says a ship to Menethil Harbor docks here from time to time.

Nat Pagle is an experienced, wry fisherman who teaches others the patience and determination fishing takes. He offers rare-fish challenges and shares his knowledge freely, while testing foul-smelling bait on a dangerous wreck. He knows the sea's monsters firsthand, warns that Tethyr is drawn to bright lights, and sends visitors to Major Mills for advice. Fishing also gives him time to reflect—and, as he admits, to drink heavily.

Doctor Gustaf VanHowzen is Alliance Trauma’s chief physician and head trauma surgeon. At Theramore, he examines prospective members through triage and trains doctors in advanced bandaging techniques. His work centers on practical medical instruction.
Dahne Pierce, a named humanoid in Dustwallow Marsh.
Balai Lok'Wein is a Theramore-area vendor of potions, scrolls, and reagents. Customers can browse his goods.
A humanoid known as Burgle Eye.
Drogoth the Roamer is an elemental found in Dustwallow Marsh.
Dart is a rare beast. It casts Raptor Charge when aggroed and Rend Flesh in combat.
Ripscale is a beast in the Barrens.
Hayoc is a beast in the Barrens.
The Rot is a creature in the Barrens.
Lord Angler is a creature in the Barrens.
Oozeworm is a beast in the Barrens.

Doctor Weavil is Narain Soothfancy’s arch-enemy, a suspicious and boastful self-styled criminal mastermind. He taunts Narain and sees through the player’s disguise, calling for his Number Two to kill.
Doctor Weavil’s flying machine is a vehicle associated with him.
A minion associated with Doctor Weavil.
Tidelord Rrurgaz is a named figure who casts spells when fighting.

Balandar Brightstar is stranded in Brackenwall Village after his ship, the Dawn Runner, ran aground. He wants his cargo recovered and his first mate Ithania freed from Theramore forces at North Point Tower. He dismisses the local ogres as useless and calls the Theramore troops privateers; once Ithania has rested and he is prepared, he plans to leave for civilization.

Ithania is the Dawn Runner's first mate, held at North Point Tower after Theramore forces seized the ship's cargo. She expects to make her own way back to Brackenwall and warns her rescuer to be careful.
Risen spirits are undead found around Brackenwall Marsh. This spirit casts Intangible Presence, marking it as ghostly and insubstantial beside the more corporeal risen husks.
Risen husks are undead found around Brackenwall Marsh. When badly wounded, a husk consumes flesh; this marks its behavior apart from the area's intangible risen spirits.

Calia Hastings is an SI:7 agent running an operation in Theramore against deserter agents. She uses exposure, altered leaflets, and an attempt to capture their leader to disrupt them, and plans further moves before reporting to Stormwind. Her account leaves the deserters' possible return to Lady Jaina's decision.

Inspector Tarem is Theramore’s investigator at the Shady Rest Inn ruins, sent to uncover how the inn was destroyed. He uses reflective powder to expose suspicious objects and markings, and his wary greeting shows little trust in those ordered to assist him. He treats the case as delicate and asks visitors to inspect the violent crime scene with respect.

Captain Darill commands at North Point Tower and regards the Grimtotems as a persistent threat to Theramore’s marsh outposts. Following Captain Vimes’s lead on the Shady Rest massacre, he seeks orders and compares recovered arms to test the Blackhoof Village connection. His response notes that the arms are unused, so another Grimtotem post may be involved; short of men, he directs the searcher to the mage Tabetha for help.

Renn McGill is an SI:7 salvage diver working around the wreckage off Dustwallow Marsh. He repairs diving gear and helps recover the ship’s cargo. As he sorts through the salvage, he first finds coins and jewelry, then recognizes enchanted manacles and realizes the cargo was a prisoner. His spoken remarks show his growing concern as the search turns from valuables to a person.

Gizzix Grimegurgle is a named resident of Mudsprocket who is trying to keep the field team supplied while the zeppelin’s supplies are delayed. He says the injuries, insects, and nearby enemies have left him short of medicines and bandages, and that wyrmtail can help heal wounds and dull pain. He is grateful for more of the herb to help keep his people going until Moxie returns with supplies.
Razbo Rustgear is a weapon and armor merchant who offers goods and repairs.

Drazzit Dripvalve helps establish Mudsprocket and welcomes aid and business contacts, including Theramore. Food and supply shortages worry him, and he depends on zeppelin cargo to support the settlement. He authorizes a bounty on Goreclaw the Ravenous but frets that raising the reward too far would exceed the town's budget.
Krixil Slogswitch sells food and drink in Mudsprocket. Krixil doubts Drazzit will find anyone to kill the raptor, noting that Drazzit has already raised the reward twice.

Brogg is a Stonemaul ogre who fled with Overlord Mok'Morokk after dragonkin destroyed his home and killed many of his friends. He wants revenge and seeks the clan banner, while also trying to lay the dead Stonemaul spirits to rest. The Mudsprocket goblins are his friends and have let him stay, though he sometimes thinks they laugh at him and finds their buildings too small.
A Witch Light found in Dustwallow Marsh.
A Defias conjuror, this hostile spellcaster uses a spell in combat.
A Grimtotem Breaker is a combatant of the Grimtotem group. Its name marks a forceful raiding role; in combat it uses a spell.
A Grimtotem Spirit-Shifter is a Grimtotem combatant whose role centers on spirit magic: it summons a spirit wolf and uses shock in combat.

A Grimtotem Destroyer is a raider at Direhorn Post, one of the Grimtotems attacking the settlers near Tabetha’s farm. Morlann’s request identifies these Grimtotems as a threat to the farm; the Destroyer uses a combat spell as well.
A Grimtotem Earthbinder is a Grimtotem combatant who uses an Earthbind Totem in battle. The title points to a binding role among the group’s fighters.

Apprentice Morlann serves Tabetha at her farm and asks for help against the Grimtotem attacks. Morlann speaks with dry impatience about lost privacy and mages who use the last of a reagent without replacing it. Morlann also shares what is known about the zeppelin wreck to the east and points travelers toward Moxie Steelgrille, the Cartel representative investigating it.

Apprentice Garion studies a captured Grimtotem totem after being wounded in an attack, but his experiments have not revealed how it works. He also shares reagents with Apprentice Morlann and tries to replace missing marsh venom before Morlann notices; Garion's own gossip grumbles about Morlann's complaints and abandoned summoning tomes.

Deserter Agitators court Theramore soldiers with invitations to reminisce about the city's former glory and offers to revive the old fight against the Horde. They praise Admiral Proudmoore and denounce Jaina's restraint as cowardice; their friendly recruiting pitch turns threatening when challenged.
Dyslix Silvergrub is a flight master who shows travelers the available air routes. When attacked, he can call an enraged gryphon or wyvern to defend himself.
A privateer, identified by a seafaring role rather than a personal name.
A Mudsprocket bruiser who serves as a fighter around the settlement.
A deserter lieutenant, an armed humanoid officer.
Garn Mathers is a named figure associated with a search for Defias orders in Dustwallow Marsh.
A Scorchscale drake, an elite dragonkin creature.
Cassa Crimsonwing is Theramore's apprentice gryphon master, learning gryphon handling from Baldruc and hoping one day to run her own gryphon stable.
A Grimtotem elder who meets intruders with magic, using spells in combat.
A Theramore patrolman captured by the Grimtotems, he thanks his rescuer when freed and fears what his captors might have done to him.

At North Point Tower, Sergeant Lukas directs Theramore's response to Grimtotem attacks. He seeks the return of captured patrols and plans to use captured raptors against the raiders. His replies show dry humor and confidence in the plan.

Moxie Steelgrille is a woman working to salvage the crashed zeppelin at Beezil’s Wreck, which carried months of supplies for Mudsprocket. Wary of a stranger sent by the hermit mages, she still accepts help: first to contain corrosive oozes, then to recover cargo. She asks for a delivery to Drazzit because she considers the wreck site too unsafe to leave.

Sergeant Amelyn welcomes visitors to Theramore and keeps an eye on local concerns. She arranges occasional checks on Swamp Eye Jarl, who reminds her of her grandfather, though locals question his sanity. She doubts Babs can repair the lighthouse alone but supports the effort for smoother shipping, and considers dock duty preferable to the front lines.
Swamp Eye Jarl describes Razorspine as a murloc near the beach north of him, carrying the large sword Jarl wants.

Mordant Grimsby is an herbalist and Jarl's friend. He came to visit Jarl and grew alarmed by the horrors at Witch Hill. He studies the risen dead for clues, concluding that they represent the land's former inhabitants and that something is corrupting and killing them. He trusts nature's remedies but doubts folk magic even as he prepares a witchbane torch. When it works, he masks his relief with a joke about Jarl's furniture.

Goreclaw the Ravenous is a feared raptor leader in the Bloodfen Burrow, described as cruel and cunning and blamed for the deaths of at least two Steamwheedle engineers. Drazzit Dripvalve has authorized a reward for whoever rids Mudsprocket of this menace.

Apothecary Cylla is a Forsaken apothecary whom a letter says was dispatched to aid the Grimtotem against their mutual enemy in Kalimdor. The letter, recovered from a Forsaken apothecary's body, describes an alliance between the Grimtotem and Lordaeron's new masters; it does not establish Cylla's own views.

Babs Fizzletorque is working to relight the old lighthouse east of Theramore, believing its lamp will help ships and goods reach the docks smoothly. She considers thresher oil a practical, if inelegant, fuel, and passes an old book about sea creatures to Michael Crowe, who collects such books.

“Dirty” Michael Crowe is a fish merchant on the Theramore docks who jokes that fish gutting is a dirty job. He collects old books and believes sailors' tales may hold truth, including the book's account of Tethyr, a sea creature said to live nearby; he points curious visitors toward Nat Pagle.

Major Mills directs Theramore’s dockside defense against Tethyr, rallying marksmen and coordinating the mortars. He admits he doubted the defenders when he first saw the beast, then praises their discipline after the fight.
A mechanical cannon associated with Theramore, a weapon emplacement rather than an individually characterized person.

Gavis Greyshield leads the Theramore deserters from their ship base. When overcome, he surrenders and pleads for his men to be spared, calling them good lads who have made a mistake; his appeal shows concern for them even as their resistance ends.

Andello Porter is an SI:7 agent at Tabetha’s Farm. A letter reporting Grimtotem cooperation with the Forsaken confirms his longstanding suspicions about Horde–Forsaken ties. He is alarmed by the military danger and the possible shift in Kalimdor’s balance of power.

Lieutenant Nath is one of Theramore’s officers. He remarks that Lieutenant Aden always volunteers for gate duty, then jokes that his own post offers a fine view of the guards and the tradesmen’s daughters. The aside gives Nath a wry, openly leering streak alongside his awareness of the garrison’s routine.

Lieutenant Khand is a Theramore officer caught on what sounds like a long watch. He asks whether someone has come to relieve him, says he is sure the time is nearly up, and admits he could use a drink or three. His dry impatience makes him seem weary of duty and ready for a break, though the exchange is conditional.

Lieutenant Aden is a Theramore officer whose chief stated responsibility is the gates, which he calls his greatest responsibility. He says he has little time for conversation unless something is urgent. When presented with an orc spy’s report, he admits he cannot read orcish well but recognizes it as a report. He comes across as pressed for time and focused on the city’s security.
A Firemane Drake is a dragonkin found in Dustwallow Marsh.

Axle is an innkeeper whose building also serves as headquarters, with manuals and blueprints stored there. He firmly tells Brogg he cannot stay, then acknowledges that Brogg will not move yet while insisting the arrangement is temporary. Axle jokes that ogres are too large.
A mill worker, one of the workforce attached to the mill.
Foreman Tionn is the mill's named foreman, a supervisory role among the people working there.
A courier serving the mill, identified separately from its workers and foreman.
Logok is an innkeeper who offers a place to sleep and goods to browse. His greeting is brief and practical: if you are hungry, you can sleep here too.

The Dustwallow Marsh Flame Warden represents the local Alliance festival flame. Its greeting welcomes visitors who have come to honor the flame, encourages them to visit Alliance fires across Alliance settlements, and urges them to desecrate Horde fires. The Warden’s festival message is openly aligned with the Alliance.

The Dustwallow Marsh Flame Keeper represents the local Horde festival flame. Its greeting welcomes visitors who have come to honor the flame, encourages them to visit Horde fires across Horde settlements, and urges them to desecrate Alliance fires. The Keeper’s festival message is openly aligned with the Horde.

Ysuria is identified as a Portal Trainer, and her teaching is expressly limited to mages. She offers instruction in conjuring a portal to Theramore, giving her role a specific destination rather than a general promise of portal training.

Horace Alder is a named Mage Trainer whose concern extends beyond his training role: he says he fears for the men of Northwatch and regrets not sending some of his students to aid them. He offers mage instruction.
Crown Hoodlums operate near Sentry Point outside Theramore. Snap Snagglebolt and Snip Snagglebolt target them in efforts to stop the Crown’s operations and destroy its chemical wagons.

place_records.text: You are in Dustwallow Marsh, a contested swamp in Kalimdor where both the Alliance and the Horde hold settlements. Brackenwall Village is Horde ground, Theramore Isle is Alliance, and Mudsprocket belongs to neither side. Crocolisks, bloodfen raptors and darkmist spiders roam the marsh, Grimtotem raiders keep attacking the Alliance tower at North Point, and the Defias have survivors from a shipwreck off the coast.

You are in Shady Rest Inn, a burned ruin in Dustwallow Marsh. Theramore's investigator, Inspector Tarem, is sifting the ashes to learn how the inn was destroyed, using reflective powder to expose suspicious markings. Rows of hoofprints lead away from the still-smoking skeleton, and a blackened iron shield hangs from the crumbling chimney.

You are in Brackenwall Village, a Horde settlement in Dustwallow Marsh with an inn, a flight master, and smiths. Overlord Mok'Morokk leads the Stonemaul ogres, and the learned ogre Draz'Zilb openly condemns Mok'Morokk for demanding service. Nazeer Bloodpike directs Horde intelligence work from here, and crocolisks and darkfang venomspitters are the nearby dangers.

You are in Swamplight Manor, a house at the eastern edge of Dustwallow Marsh where the eccentric cook Swamp Eye Jarl lives. His friend Mordant Grimsby, an herbalist, came to visit and was alarmed by the horrors at Witch Hill. He studies the risen dead there for clues about what is corrupting the land.
You are in Bloodfen Burrow, a den in Dustwallow Marsh where bloodfen lashtails and razormaws lurk. Goreclaw the Ravenous is the one named beast among them.
You are in Darkmist Cavern, an old mine northwest of Brackenwall Village that darkmist spiders have taken over. Silkspinners, spiders and recluses hold its tunnels.

You are in Beezil's Wreck, a crash site in Dustwallow Marsh where a zeppelin went down carrying months of supplies for Mudsprocket. Moxie Steelgrille is salvaging what she can and is wary of strangers sent by the hermit mages. Acidic and bubbling swamp oozes threaten to corrode the wreckage, while giant darkfang spiders and drywallow daggermaws roam nearby.
You are in Witch Hill, a stretch of Dustwallow Marsh where risen spirits and risen husks shamble about. Noxious flayers, darkfang venomspitters and crocolisks are the other dangers here.

You are in Sentry Point, Alliance ground in Dustwallow Marsh, an outpost near the Dreadmurk Shore. Captain Wymor leads Theramore's inquiry into Defias survivors from a shipwreck off the coast, who were all wearing red bandanas. Guards are posted here, and patrols have reported the survivors.

You are in North Point Tower, an Alliance tower in Dustwallow Marsh where Captain Darill and Sergeant Lukas hold out against Grimtotem raiders. The raiders keep launching assaults on the tower and have captured patrols, and Lukas plans to turn captured raptors against them. Ithania, first mate of the Dawn Runner, is held here after Theramore forces seized the ship's cargo.
You are in Lost Point, a part of Dustwallow Marsh where Theramore deserters roam. A deserter lieutenant and Balos Jacken are among the ones found here.

You are in Bluefen, a stretch of Dustwallow Marsh east of Brackenwall Village, where Theramore infiltrators spy on the Horde at Brackenwall Village. Withervine creepers, ragers and mire beasts are the main dangers, and Drogoth the Roamer is a named threat.
You are in Stonemaul Ruins, the old home of the Stonemaul ogres, who were driven out by dragons. Firemane scouts and ash tails, and searing whelps and hatchlings, now roam the ruins.

You are in The Den of Flame, a former Stonemaul ogre mound in Dustwallow Marsh that is now crawling with dragonkin. Firemane scouts and ash tails patrol it, with drywallow daggermaws and a darkfang creeper among them.

You are in The Dragonmurk, an area of Dustwallow Marsh east of Mudsprocket. Searing hatchlings and whelps, Firemane ash tails and scalebanes, and drywallow daggermaws roam here, and bloodfen lashtails are common. Wyrmtail, a herb the Mudsprocket goblins need, grows here.

You are in Wyrmbog, an area of Dustwallow Marsh east of Mudsprocket. Firemane flamecallers and scalebanes, drywallow daggermaws, and searing whelps and hatchlings crowd it, and a scorchscale drake has been seen. Wyrmtail grows here as well.

You are in Blackhoof Village, a Dustwallow Marsh settlement where Grimtotem breakers, spirit-shifters and elders are a constant danger, with withervine creepers among them. A Theramore patrolman captured by the Grimtotems is here, and he thanks anyone who frees him.

You are in Theramore Isle, the Alliance town of Theramore in Dustwallow Marsh, ruled by Lady Jaina Proudmoore. Captain Garran Vimes investigates the Shady Rest Inn destruction and the murder of the Hyal family, and watches for suspected Horde spies. Its flight master, inn and stable master serve travelers, though privateers and coral sharks lurk in its waters.
You are in Dustwallow Bay, an area of Dustwallow Marsh. Murk threshers, and muckshell clackers and scrabblers, gather here, and darkfang creepers, venomspitters and giant spiders are also here.
You are in Tidefury Cove, an area of Dustwallow Marsh. Muckshell pincers, scrabblers and clackers gather here in numbers, with giant darkfang spiders among them. Hayoc and Lord Angler also roam it.

You are in Dreadmurk Shore, an area of Dustwallow Marsh where Mirefin murlocs and Defias divers work the water. Renn McGill, an SI:7 salvage diver, repairs diving gear and helps recover cargo from the wreckage. Defias rummagers are picking through the same wreckage.

You are in Alcaz Island, an island in Dustwallow Marsh that is believed to hold the key to the Defias' mystery. Strashaz hydras, serpent guards, myrmidons, sirens and warriors are dangerous here, along with minions of Doctor Weavil.
You are in The Quagmire, an area of Dustwallow Marsh. Mottled drywallow crocolisks crowd it, with darkfang creepers, noxious shredders, drywallow daggermaws and snappers, and bubbling swamp oozes.

You are in The Great Sea, an area of Dustwallow Marsh. Muckshell pincers, scrabblers and clackers gather here, and Theramore deserters with a deserter lieutenant are among the dangers, with Gavis Greyshield also present. Young murk threshers are found in these waters too.

You are in Mudsprocket, a goblin settlement in Dustwallow Marsh that belongs to neither side, with an inn, a flight master and repairs. Drazzit Dripvalve helped establish it and depends on zeppelin cargo, and the crash has left its medicines and bandages short. Brogg, a Stonemaul ogre, lives here seeking revenge on the black dragonkin.
You are in Direhorn Post in Dustwallow Marsh. Grimtotem destroyers and earthbinders haunt it, along with crocolisks, darkfang creepers, a drywallow daggermaw and a giant darkfang spider.
You are in Nat's Landing in Dustwallow Marsh. Nat Pagle, a wry fisherman who has worked at it for twenty or thirty years, sells his wares here and knows the sea's monsters well.

You are in Tabetha's Farm in Dustwallow Marsh, where Tabetha mentors spellcasters and her apprentices Morlann and Garion work with her. Grimtotem attacks keep troubling the farm, and Garion is studying a captured Grimtotem totem without yet learning how it works. A spirit healer here offers a return to life for a price.
